Thanks Priya — notes below, keeping language operational and evidence pointers. I’ve attached a simplified VPC diagram for the Private option.

Hosted (Redwood-hosted multi-tenant):
- Control plane: Redwood-owned (management, orchestration, monitoring).
- Data plane: Customer data may traverse shared infrastructure; we logically isolate workloads via tenant IDs and runtime namespaces.
- Keys: Redwood-managed KMS by default; CMK (customer-managed) not available in multi-tenant hosted.
- Network isolation: TLS in transit; customer endpoints terminate at Redwood-managed ingress. No customer VPC peering.
- Logs / audit access: Aggregated audit logs in our SOC2 system; we provide per-customer log exports on request (subject to retention policy).
- Evidence: SOC2 report (available under NDA), hosted-runtime runbook, example tenant log export.

Dedicated (single-tenant / reserved capacity):
- Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane but tenant-dedicated runtime instances; orchestration still by Redwood unless "Private Control Plane" option is chosen.
- Data plane: Dedicated GPU pools assigned to the customer; data residency controlled by region selection.
- Keys: Customer can bring CMK for encryption-at-rest in Dedicated when configured (we integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs).
- Network isolation: Optional VPC peering or private connectivity (Direct Connect / VPN) depending on customer environment.
- Logs / audit access: Per-tenant audit streams; we can ship logs into customer S3 or customer-managed logging endpoint.
- Evidence: Dedicated deployment checklist, KMS-integration guide, per-tenant logging sample.

Private / VPC / On-prem:
- Control plane: Two variants — (a) Redwood-managed control plane with customer VPC (Private SaaS), or (b) fully customer-hosted control plane (on-prem). Specify which in SIG answers.
- Data plane: Runs entirely in customer VPC or on-prem network; no shared compute.
- Keys: Customer retains exclusive KMS control in standard Private configurations; Redwood can optionally manage keys if customer requests and contractually agreed.
- Network isolation: Full VPC isolation, direct private connectivity, and customer network policies apply.
- Logs / audit access: Customer has direct access to runtime logs; Redwood can provide collector agents or ship logs on customer’s routing.
- Evidence: VPC architecture diagram (attached), private-deployment runbook, KMS configuration example.

Edge cases / notes:
- Some Dedicated customers opt for "bring your own KMS" which changes the operational responsibility for key rotation.
- Control plane data (management telemetry) may be visible to Redwood operators unless a fully customer-hosted control plane is used. Call that out explicitly.

Thanks Karthik — great breakdown. Below are suggested short sentences we can drop into the SIG answers (auditor-friendly, non-contractual). I kept each row to one sentence so the Faro team can paste directly into the SIG matrix.

Hosted (multi-tenant):
"Redwood operates the control plane and shared runtime infrastructure; customers are responsible for their own data and access controls within their tenant; Redwood retains responsibility for platform patching, monitoring, and operational telemetry."

Dedicated (single-tenant):
"Redwood manages the control plane and provisions tenant-dedicated runtime resources in the region requested by the customer; customers may integrate their KMS and private network connections subject to the dedicated deployment configuration."

Private / VPC / On-prem:
"Customer-managed deployment: runtime and data flow reside in the customer's VPC or on-prem environment; customers retain administrative control over network, keys, and logs unless otherwise contracted."

One small legal note: avoid saying "we never see customer data" — instead say "Redwood does not use customer data for model training and operates under the data handling commitments in our agreement." I recommend that phrasing for the SIG.

If this looks good I’ll polish into a one-paragraph summary per mode and hand it back to Priya for final formatting.

— Grace
Head of Product Compliance
Redwood Inference
